extracted.intended_audience: offshore renewable energy developers, potential bidders, lessees/grant holders, and their legal/compliance teams; BOEM program staff
extracted.subtask_description: Federal proposed rule text (30 CFR part 585) specifying requirements, processes, definitions, and evaluation criteria for leasing, permitting, auctions, and compliance for offshore (OCS) renewable energy activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balancing program goals (§585.102)
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM will ensure that any activities authorized in this part are carried out in a manner that provides for and balances the following goals, none of which inherently outweighs or supplants any other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activities must be implemented with balanced consideration of the enumerated program goals (goals list appears in the regulation). No single goal is inherently dominant; BOEM must weigh goals when authorizing activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions allowing departures from regulations (§585.103)
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM may prescribe or approve a departure from these regulations when BOEM deems the departure necessary because the applicable provision(s) as applied to a specific circumstance: (1) are impractical or unduly burdensome and the departure is necessary to achieve the intended objectives of the renewable energy program; (2) fail to conserve the natural resources of the OCS; (3) fail to protect life (including human and wildlife), property, or the marine, coastal, or human environment; or (4) fail to protect sites, structures, or objects of historical or archaeological significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for departures must demonstrate one of the listed failings or impracticability relative to the regulation as applied to the specific circumstance; BOEM will evaluate whether departure is necessary to achieve program objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorization requirement to produce electricity on the OCS (§585.104)
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as otherwise authorized by law, it is unlawful for any person to construct, operate, or maintain any facility to produce, transport, or support generation of electricity or other energy product derived from a renewable energy resource on any part of the OCS, except in accordance with the terms of a lease, easement, or ROW issued under the OCS Lands Act. For the purposes of this section, site assessment activities do not produce, transport, or support the generation of electricity or other energy product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction/operation for commercial generation requires a BOEM lease/easement/ROW; site assessment activities are carved out and are not considered production for this prohibition.

rubrics_metrics.name: General lessee/grant holder responsibilities (§585.105)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comply with all applicable laws and regulations, the terms of your lease or grant under this part, reports, notices, and approved plans prepared under this part, and any conditions imposed by BOEM through its review of any of these reports, notices, and approved plans, as provided in this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lessee/grant holder compliance obligation is comprehensive: statutory/regulatory requirements, lease/grant terms, approved plans, and conditions set by BOEM during reviews must be followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualification criteria to acquire or hold a lease or grant (§585.106)
rubrics_metrics.description: You may acquire or hold a lease or grant under this part if you can demonstrate that you have the technical and financial capabilities to conduct the activities authorized by the lease or grant and you are among specified eligible entities (including states). BOEM may disqualify parties after notice and opportunity to be heard if they no longer meet qualification requirements or have engaged in violations, illegal activity, anti-competitive or collusive behavior, fraud, or misrepresentation and have not taken timely remedial action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must demonstrate technical and financial capability; BOEM can determine ineligibility for specified misconduct or failure to meet qualifications. While ineligible, a party cannot participate in BOEM lease/grant issuance processes even as an agent; eligibility can be restored by completing specified remedial action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citizenship/residency proof for individuals (§585.107(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual must submit a written statement of citizenship status attesting to U.S. citizenship. It does not need to be notarized nor give the age of the individual. A resident alien may submit a photocopy of the form issued by the appropriate Federal immigration authority evidencing legal status as a resident alien.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individual applicants must provide simple attestation of citizenship or copy of immigration documentation for resident aliens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document submission method (§585.110)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise stated, you must submit one electronic copy of all plans, applications, reports, or notices required by this part to BOEM. BOEM will inform you if it requires paper copies of specific documents. Unless stated otherwise, documents should be submitted to the relevant contacts listed on the BOEM website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default method is electronic submission of one copy; check BOEM notices for any exceptions requiring paper copies and follow listed contacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Bidding credit(s) (§585.112)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bidding credit(s) means the value assigned by BOEM, expressed in monetary terms, to the factors or actions demonstrated, or committed to, by a bidder at a BOEM lease auction during the competitive lease award process. The type(s) and value(s) of any bidding credit(s) awarded to any given bidder will be set forth in the Final Sale Notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bidding credits are non-monetary factors converted to monetary value as described in the FSN; their availability/value will be specified in the FSN.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Commercial activities (§585.112)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commercial activities means, under renewable energy leases and grants, all activities associated with the generation, storage, or transmission of electricity or other energy product from a renewable energy project on the OCS, and where such electricity or other energy product is intended for distribution, sale, or other commercial use, except for electricity or other energy product distributed or sold pursuant either to technology-testing activities on a limited lease or facilities testing on a commercial lease needed to prepare a final FIR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies which activities constitute commercial operations versus testing or technology demonstrations; includes development life-cycle activities (characterization, construction, decommissioning).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Commercial operations (§585.112)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commercial operations means the generation of electricity or other energy product for commercial use, sale, and distribution on a commercial lease, but does not mean either generation needed to prepare a final FIR or generation for testing purposes, provided the electricity generated for such testing is not sold on a commercial basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes commercial generation from testing or pre-FIR generation; affects timing of certain obligations and data disclosure triggers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Critical Safety System (§585.112)
rubrics_metrics.description: Critical Safety System means safety systems and equipment designed to prevent or ameliorate major accidents that could result in harm to health, safety, or the environment in the area of your facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies safety-critical equipment that BOEM will regard as necessary to prevent major accidents; relevant for design, inspection, and enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Engineered foundation (§585.112)
rubrics_metrics.description: Engineered foundation means any structure installed on the seabed using a fixed-bottom foundation constructed according to a professional engineering design (based on an assessment of relevant sedimentary, meteorological, and oceanographic conditions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets standard that fixed-bottom foundations must be professional-engineering-designed with consideration of site conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Fabrication (§585.112)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fabrication means the cutting, fitting, welding, or other assembly of project elements of a custom design conforming to project-specific requirements. Fabrication does not include the procurement of discrete parts of the project that are commercially available in standardized form or with type-certified components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes custom assembly/fabrication work from procurement of standardized components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Lease area (§585.112)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lease area means an area on the OCS that BOEM has identified for leasing for potential development of renewable energy resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to define geographic scope of leases and related processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Multiple factor auction (§585.112)
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple factor auction means an auction that involves the use of bidding credits to incentivize goals or actions that support public policy objectives or maximize public benefits through the competitive leasing auction process. For any multiple factor auction, the monetary value of the bidding credits, if any, would be added to the value of the cash bid to determine the highest bidder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how non-cash factors are monetized and combined with cash bids to rank bidders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Project Design Envelope (PDE) (§585.112)
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Design Envelope (PDE) means a reasonable range of design parameters proposed in a lessee's plan for components of the project, such as type, dimensions, and number of wind turbine generators; foundation type; location of the export cable route; location of an onshore substation; location of the grid connection point; and construction methods and timing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PDE concept allows flexibility in proposed design parameters while bounding the project for environmental and regulatory review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Provisional winner (§585.112)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisional winner means a bidder that BOEM determines at the conclusion of the auction to have submitted the winning bid. The provisional winner becomes the winning bidder after the favorable completion of BOEM's bid review, Department of Justice antitrust review, bidder obligations under §585.225, and any appeals process under §585.118(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auction winner status is provisional until BOEM completes post-auction reviews and any appeal processes; provisional winner has specific post-auction obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Receipt timing for mailed/electronic documents (§585.112)
rubrics_metrics.description: Receipt, as used in this part to describe the time when a document is received by any party in the absence of documentation to the contrary, is deemed to have taken place: 5-business days after the date the document was given to the U.S. Postal Service... or, on the date on which the document was properly addressed and sent electronically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes deemed receipt timings for mailed and electronic submissions where timing triggers regulatory time periods or consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Site assessment activities (§585.112)
rubrics_metrics.description: Site assessment activities mean those initial activities conducted to assess an area on the OCS, such as resource assessment surveys (e.g., meteorological and oceanographic) or technology testing, involving the installation of bottom-founded facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that certain early-stage installations for characterization/testing are site assessment activities and distinguishes them from commercial activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data disclosure timing for commercial lease data (§585.113(b)(1)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have a commercial lease, then BOEM will review data and information for possible release: 3 years after the initiation of commercial operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes a specific time threshold (3 years after commercial operations begin) for BOEM to consider releasing data obtained under the part.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRA information collection purposes by subpart (§585.114(e)(2)-(11))
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM lists the reasons for collecting information and how it is used for each subpart: e.g., Subpart B—to enable BOEM to publish a proposed five-year leasing schedule; Subpart C—to provide information to determine when to use competitive processes and auction formats; Subpart D—to issue ROW/RUE grants; Subpart E—to ensure compliance with lease/grant administration; Subpart F—to ensure payments and financial assurance compliance; Subpart G—to enable BOEM to comply with NEPA, CZMA, and other laws and ensure safety; Subpart H—to review final design/fabrication/installation for compliance; Subpart I—to ensure lease and grant operations are conducted safely and in compliance; Subpart J—to determine decommissioning compliance and site clearance; Subpart K—to review RUE design/installation/operation to ensure safety and compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each subpart's information collection is tied to a specific regulatory or programmatic purpose (leasing schedule, issuing leases, grants, safety, environmental compliance, decommissioning, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons BOEM may publish a Request for Information (RFI) (§585.116)
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM may publish an RFI to: (a) solicit information from industry, State and local agencies, federally recognized Tribes, and other interested entities for evaluating the offshore renewable energy industry, including identification of potential challenges or obstacles; (b) to assess interest in leasing all or part of the OCS for activities authorized in this part; (c) to determine whether there is competitive interest in a specific OCS renewable energy proposal (e.g., unsolicited requests); and (d) to seek other information BOEM needs for the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RFIs are a tool to gather information for program refinement, leasing interest assessment, competitive interest determination, and other informational needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal rights and procedures (§585.118)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any party adversely affected by a final decision issued by BOEM under this part may appeal to the Interior Board of Land Appeals (IBLA) under part 590 and 43 CFR part 4, subpart E; final decisions remain in effect during appeals unless a stay is granted. A bidder adversely affected by BOEM's determination of a provisional winner may appeal to the BOEM Director (not to IBLA) within 15 business days after receipt, accompanied by a statement of reasons; the Director will provide the provisional winner a reasonable opportunity to respond and will issue a written determination that is not appealable to IBLA. BOEM will not execute a lease or grant until the 15-business-day appeal period closes and all timely filed appeals are resolved. The Office of Hearings and Appeals' review authority does not apply to provisional winner selection decisions or the Director's final determination on those appeals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies appeal fora, timelines (15 business days for provisional-winner appeals), required statement of reasons, opportunity to respond, effect on lease execution, and limits on further review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewable energy leasing schedule timing and contents (§585.150)
rubrics_metrics.description: At least once every 2 years, the Secretary will publish a schedule with a list of locations under consideration for leasing, along with a projection of when lease sales are anticipated to occur for the 5-year period following the schedule's publication. This schedule will include a general description of the area, the calendar year projected for each sale, and reasons for any changes made to the previous schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedule must be updated biennially, include 5-year projections, descriptive information, and justification for changes; any proposed sale remains subject to applicable regulations and environmental reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of leases BOEM may issue (§585.202)
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM may issue commercial or limited leases for OCS activities under §585.104. BOEM may issue a lease for OCS renewable energy research activities under §585.238.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leases may be commercial, limited, or for research depending on activity type and regulatory criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation before issuance of leases (§585.203)
rubrics_metrics.description: For leases issued under this part, BOEM will coordinate and consult with relevant Federal agencies, the Governor of any affected State, the executive of any affected local government, and any affected Indian Tribe, as directed by subsections 8(p)(4) and (7) of the OCS Lands Act or other relevant Federal laws. Federal statutes requiring consultation include the ESA and MSA. BOEM also engages with state and tribal historic preservation officers pursuant to the NHPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-issuance consultation is required with a broad set of stakeholders and agencies, and statutory consultation obligations (ESA, MSA, NHPA) guide the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitive lease award process steps (§585.210)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each competitive lease award process will include the following steps: (1) Call for Information and Nominations (Call); (2) Area Identification; (3) Proposed Sale Notice (PSN); (4) Final Sale Notice (FSN); (5) Auction; (6) Lease Award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM will follow these sequential steps in a competitive process; public notices and opportunities for input are embedded in the process steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents and uses of the Call (§585.211)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Call is a notice requesting responses from stakeholders interested in bidding and comments from interested/affected parties; it may include the areas preliminarily identified for leasing; requests for comments on geological conditions, archaeological sites, multiple uses, feasibility, possible lease terms; requests for bidder nominations including specific OCS blocks, respondent objectives and proposed means, preliminary schedule, coordination info, documentation of qualifications, relevant energy/environmental data, and other requested information. Respondents have 45 calendar days (minimum 30) to reply. BOEM may use responses to identify lease areas, develop lease provisions, inform environmental analyses, and determine competitive interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Call responses must include specified nomination and informational elements; response period defaults to 45 days unless otherwise stated; BOEM uses responses for selection, stipulations, NEPA/other analyses, and to decide if competitive interest exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Area identification criteria and process (§585.212)
rubrics_metrics.description: Area identification is the process by which BOEM delineates one or more OCS areas for leasing consideration based on an area's relevant attributes, such as other uses of the area, environmental factors or characteristics, stakeholder comments, industry nominations, feasibility for development, and other relevant information. BOEM will evaluate potential effects on human, marine, and coastal environments and the feasibility of development and may develop mitigation measures and hold public hearings. At the end of area identification, BOEM may offer selected areas for leasing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Area selection weighs multiple attributes (uses, environment, stakeholder input, feasibility) and can result in mitigation/stipulations; public hearings may be held as part of the environmental analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed Sale Notice (PSN) required content (§585.213)
rubrics_metrics.description: At a minimum, the PSN will include or describe: proposed lease areas (size/location); proposed lease terms and conditions (rental/operating fee rates); other payment requirements; proposed performance requirements including lease stipulations and mitigation measures; steps a bidder must take to obtain/maintain eligibility (financial forms, bid deposits); availability/potential value of bidding credits and required actions to obtain them; detailed auction format and procedures (§585.223); maximum number or sets of lease areas per bidder if applicable; lease award procedures (how/when awarded and executed, handling unsuccessful bids); copy of or reference to official BOEM lease form; and other relevant matters. PSN public comment period is 60 calendar days (minimum 30).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PSN must provide comprehensive pre-auction information to enable informed comments and bidder preparation; the PSN can be used to gauge continued bidder interest and to solicit objections to terms that may preclude participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Sale Notice (FSN) required content and timing (§585.214)
rubrics_metrics.description: FSN must be published at least 30 calendar days before each prospective auction and describe final auction details including leases to be offered (areas, terms, payments, performance requirements), steps to ensure bidder eligibility, availability/value of bidding credits, detailed auction format/procedures, maximum number/sets of lease areas per bidder if applicable, lease award procedures, copy/reference to the official BOEM lease form, and other relevant matters. FSN terms may differ from PSN terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FSN finalizes auction and lease terms and must be published at least 30 days before auction; bidders must follow FSN-established eligibility and procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessing whether competitive interest remains (§585.215)
rubrics_metrics.description: If BOEM has reason to believe competitive interest no longer exists before auction, BOEM may issue a notice requesting information regarding competitive interest and consider respondents' comments. BOEM may end the competitive process if it determines competitive interest no longer exists. If only a single party remains interested, BOEM may proceed either with the auction or with the noncompetitive process following payment of the acquisition fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM actively checks for competitive interest and may convert to noncompetitive procedures or proceed with auction depending on responses; payment of acquisition fee is required for noncompetitive award when only one interested party remains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bidding credits awarding and use rules (§585.216)
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM will determine the highest bid taking into account the combined value of cash and non-monetary components (bidding credits). The PSN and FSN will explain: eligibility and application requirements; the value of each bidding credit (sum certain or percentage of cash bid); and procedures for applying credits to bids. Eligibility must be established in advance and may be based on actions undertaken or commitments to be undertaken if BOEM agrees. BOEM may offer bidding credits for power purchase agreements, renewable energy credits/subsidies eligibility, development agreements facilitating shared transmission, technical merit/timeliness/financing, environmental considerations/public benefits/compatibility with State/local needs, developer commitments facilitating OCS goals, or any other factor identified by BOEM. Before the auction BOEM determines each bidder's eligibility and value of bidding credits and informs each eligible bidder. A provisional winner awarded bidding credits must pay an amount equal to the cash component of its winning bid less any bid deposit retained by BOEM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bidding credits convert non-monetary public-benefit factors into bid value; rules on eligibility, valuation, and application are specified in PSN/FSN and determined before the auction. Provisional winners receiving credits still must remit the net cash component as described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auction fairness and methods (§585.220)
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM will award leases competitively using an objective, fair, reasonable, and competitive auction process that provides a fair return to the United States. As described in the FSN, leases will be awarded to the highest bidder. BOEM may use any analog or digital method to conduct the auction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auctions must be procedurally fair and designed to produce a fair return; BOEM has flexibility in auction technologies/methods but must follow FSN-described procedures and selection of highest bidder methodology (including bidding credits where applicable).
